newsitem.title: USA: U.S. oil shares rise on prospect for consolidation.
newsitem.headline: U.S. oil shares rise on prospect for consolidation.

text.p: Shares of U.S. oil companies rose on views that a potential alliance between Texaco Inc and Shell Oil Co could spur more consolidation of refining and marketing operations.

Shares of Texaco rallied 1-3/8 to 97 after it confirmed that it was discussing a joint venture with Shell. The Wall Street Journal Monday reported that the two companies are considering joining U.S. refining and marketing operations.
Mobil Corp, which already has a downstream joint venture with British Petroleum Co Plc in Europe, gained 2-1/8 to 118-7/8.

"I think everybody's going to take a look at it. This is a mature industry with little control over pricing and little control over volume. The only thing under a company's control is costs," said Fred Leuffer of Bear Stearns & Co.
Amoco Corp rose 3/4 to 72 and Phillips Petroleum Co gained 1/2 to 43-1/2.
The prospect of an alliance between the two industry giants comes amid difficult times for the refining industry, which has long been plagued with high costs and low profit margins.
"Obviously this is an important event for the industry. It's clearly a trend," said one analyst who did not want to be identified.

Analysts believe the future of the refining industry will be governed by similar alliances rather than complete unions like the one announced last month between Diamond Shamrock Inc and Ultramar Corp.

However, they also noted that Texaco and Shell are still in the negotiation phase and that an actual deal has not been set. A similar potential venture between Phillips and Conoco Inc collapsed earlier this year after the two firms were unable to agree on significant issues.
